answer: To resist sybil attacks, every agent must deposit a stake that funds a continuous sequential hash-chain proof over a unique hardware enclave. The chain must bridge the full epoch duration; missing a step or sharing the enclave root across identities causes immediate forfeiture. An attacker creating many identities faces linear capital lockup plus distinct physical hardware costs that grow with each additional sybil, making mass farming economically unviable beyond a small ocean of genuine participants who reach the summit of sustained participation.
